data.name: ProblemAccessDenied
data.value: Windows denied access to the CUSTOS service channel.

data.name: ProblemVersionMismatch
data.value: The interface and the service are different versions. Reinstall CUSTOS.

data.value: Pause or resume the running task

data.name: ToolCardHint
data.value: Show or hide the task card

data.name: NoConnection
data.value:
{0}
The window connects again by itself as soon as the service answers.

data.name: ConfirmDelete
data.value:
Delete the task «{0}»?
The backups it has made stay where they are.

data.name: ProblemNoConnection
data.value: No connection to the CUSTOS service.

data.name: ProblemNoAnswer
data.value: The service did not answer in time.

data.name: ProblemRequestFailed
data.value: The service could not do it: {0}

data.name: ProblemUnexpected
data.value:
Something went wrong in the CUSTOS window: {0}
Backups go on: the service does not depend on the window. The details are written to {1}. If this repeats, close the interface from the tray menu and open it again.

data.name: CardNoSelection
data.value: Select a task in the list

data.name: HistoryEmpty
data.value: This task has not run yet.

data.name: HistorySelectTask
data.value: Select a task to see its runs.

data.name: NothingQueued
data.value: Nothing to run: no task is switched on.

data.name: TrayWarning
data.value: the last run of «{0}» needs a look

data.name: TypeFullHint
data.value: Every time all files are copied. Reliable and simple, but slow, and takes more space.

data.name: TypeIncrementalHint
data.value: Only the files changed since the last backup of any type are copied. Fast and thrifty, but a restore needs the full backup and all incremental ones after it.

data.name: TypeDifferentialHint
data.value: The files changed since the last full backup are copied. The backup grows each time, but a restore needs only the full and the last differential backup.

data.name: TypeMirrorHint
data.value: The destination folder is kept the same as the sources: only new and changed files are copied. No compression and no separate folders, the files open as they are.

data.name: MirrorExact
data.value: Exact: files deleted in the sources are deleted from the mirror too

data.name: MirrorSafe
data.value: Safe: replaced and deleted files are moved to the folder _custos_deleted and kept for

data.name: MirrorNote
data.value: Only files CUSTOS put into the mirror are ever deleted; other files in that folder stay. If a folder of the sources cannot be read, nothing is deleted that time.

data.name: ForceMonthDay
data.value: On the day of the month

data.name: ForceFullNote
data.value: Only for incremental and differential tasks. The first backup is always full, and so is a backup whose full one is missing in the destination.

data.name: SourcesNote
data.value: Folders and files to back up. A network folder can be read under its own account.

data.name: KeepTopDirHelp
data.value: On: D:\Data is copied into <backup>\Data\… Off: the contents of D:\Data go straight into <backup>\…

data.name: ErrorNoSources
data.value: Add at least one source or database server, or switch the task off.

data.name: SourceAccountHelp
data.value: The network folder is read under this account. «Service account» is the account of this computer itself: it works in a domain if the computer may read the share; a NAS in a workgroup usually needs a user account.

data.name: SourceNote
data.value: Files open in other programs are read from a shadow copy when VSS is on for the task (page «Advanced»). Network folders are read without VSS.

data.name: ErrorPathNotAbsolute
data.value: «{0}» is not a full path. Enter it with the drive letter or as \\server\share.

data.name: ErrorNotUnc
data.value: «{0}» is not a network path. A network folder starts with two backslashes, for example \\server\share.

data.name: ErrorUncNeedsNetwork
data.value: «{0}» is a network path: choose «Network folder».

data.name: DestinationsNote
data.value: Where the backups go. With several destinations the files are read once and written to all of them; if one fails, the others still get the backup.

data.name: DestinationKindHelp
data.value: Local folder: a folder on a disk of this computer. Network folder: a path like \\server\share\folder, opened under the chosen account. USB disk: found by its volume label, so a new drive letter does not matter.

data.name: DestinationUsbHelp
data.value: The disk is found by its volume label, so its drive letter does not matter. The list offers the labels of the disks connected now. The folder is a path on that disk without the drive letter, for example Backup\Office.

data.name: DestinationAccountHelp
data.value: The network folder is opened under this account; files on this computer are still read by the service. «Service account» is the account of this computer itself: it works in a domain if the computer may write to the share; a NAS in a workgroup usually needs a user account.

data.name: DestinationLater
data.value: This type of destination arrives in a later version of CUSTOS. Until then the task writes nothing there and reports an error for it.

data.name: SeparateFolders
data.value: A separate folder for each backup

data.name: SeparateFoldersHelp
data.value: On: each backup goes into its own folder, named by the template below, and old backups are deleted by the retention rules. Off: the files go straight into the destination folder and are updated there at each run; earlier versions are not kept.

data.name: NameTemplateHelp
data.value: The name of the folder (or archive) of each backup. Pick a variant from the list or type your own. {task} is the task name, {yyyy}-{MM}-{dd} {HH}-{mm} the date and time of the run, {type} Full, Incremental or Differential, {computer} the computer name.

data.name: LayoutMirrorNote
data.value: A mirror writes the files straight into the destination folder, without folders per backup.

data.name: ErrorNoDestinations
data.value: Add at least one destination, or switch the task off.

data.name: ErrorDestinationFolderRequired
data.value: Enter the folder of the destination.

data.name: ErrorUsbLabelRequired
data.value: Enter the label of the USB disk.

data.name: ErrorTemplateRequired
data.value: Enter the name of the backup folders.

data.name: ScheduleTimesHelp
data.value: One or more times separated by commas, for example 12:30, 21:00.

data.name: ScheduleMonthDaysHelp
data.value: Numbers from 1 to 31 separated by commas, for example 1, 15. A month without that day (31 in April) has no run: for the end of every month tick «last day of the month».

data.name: ScheduleCatchUpHelp
data.value: If the computer was off or asleep at the time of a run, the task runs once when the computer is back. Only the last missed run of the past 7 days counts.

data.name: ScheduleTimeZoneNote
data.value: Times are the local time of this computer.

data.name: ErrorBadTime
data.value: «{0}» is not a time. Use HH:MM, for example 21:30.

data.name: ErrorBadMonthDay
data.value: «{0}» is not a day of the month (1 to 31).

data.name: ErrorNoWeekdays
data.value: Tick at least one day of the week.

data.name: ErrorNoMonthDays
data.value: Enter at least one day of the month, or tick «last day of the month».

data.name: RetentionMirrorNote
data.value: A mirror is one copy that is kept up to date, so there is nothing to delete here. How long a safe mirror keeps replaced and deleted files is set on the «Basic» page.

data.name: RetentionCountHint
data.value: A full backup is deleted together with the incremental and differential backups made after it, never on its own.

data.name: RetentionAgeHint
data.value: A full backup is deleted only when every backup made after it on top of it is old too, so the backups that stay can always be restored.

data.name: RetentionGfs
data.value: Grandfather-father-son: keep the last backup of each day, week and month

data.name: RetentionGfsHint
data.value: For example 7, 4 and 12 keep a backup for each of the last 7 days, 4 weeks and 12 months. A backup that a kept one builds on (its full backup, the incremental ones before it) stays too. One task with a forced full backup and this mode replaces the pair "daily" and "weekly" tasks.

data.name: RetentionGfsEmpty
data.value: Grandfather-father-son: keep at least one daily, weekly or monthly backup.

data.name: RetentionRulesText
data.value: • The last successful full backup is never deleted. • If a run ends with an error, nothing is deleted. • The backups are found by looking into the destination itself, so the ones made before a reinstall count too. • Retention works with archives and with «A separate folder for each backup». One shared folder and a mirror are updated in place and have nothing to delete.

data.name: FiltersNote
data.value: They apply to all sources of the task. Masks are separated by semicolons: * stands for any characters, ? for one character.

data.name: FilterIncludeHelp
data.value: If set, only the files matching these masks are copied, for example *.docx; *.xlsx. Empty: all files.

data.name: FilterExcludeHelp
data.value: The files matching these masks are not copied, for example *.bak; Thumbs.db.

data.name: FilterExcludeDirsHelp
data.value: One folder per line; it is skipped with everything inside. A name (Temp, Cache) is skipped everywhere; a path from the source folder (Projects\Old) or a full path only in that place. «Browse…» adds a full path.

data.name: SkipTempHelp
data.value: Files that Windows marks as temporary (the «temporary» attribute). Masks like *.tmp go into «Skip files».

data.name: EventsNote
data.value: Programs and scripts run as SYSTEM, without a window. An event counts as done well when the program ends with code 0. What it prints goes to the run log.

data.name: EventsAbortOnPre
data.value: Stop the task if an event before fails

data.name: EventsPostNote
data.value: The events after run even when the backup failed or was stopped, so that a service stopped before starts again. A failed event after is a warning.

data.name: EventTimeoutHelp
data.value: A program still running after this time is stopped together with everything it started, and the event counts as failed. For a service: how long to wait until it has stopped or started.

data.name: EventProgramHelp
data.value: .exe runs directly, .bat and .cmd through cmd.exe, .ps1 through PowerShell (execution policy Bypass). Variables like %SystemRoot% are filled in. For a service, enter its name as the list shows it (the service name, not the display name).

data.name: ErrorEventServiceRequired
data.value: Enter the name of the service.

data.name: AfterNote
data.value: If other tasks wait in the queue, this waits until the queue is empty. Everyone signed in then sees a 60-second countdown with «Cancel». Nothing happens after a run that was stopped.

data.name: VssHelp
data.value: Windows takes a snapshot of the disks with the sources, and files open in other programs (mail databases, accounting databases and the like) are copied from it in a consistent state. Works for disks of this computer only.

data.name: VssContinue
data.value: copy without it, with a warning

data.name: ReadRetriesHelp
data.value: How many more times to try a file that could not be read, 2 seconds apart. 0: no retries.

data.name: PriorityHelp
data.value: When several tasks wait in the queue, the one with the higher number runs first. Tasks run one at a time.

data.name: AccountDomainNote
data.value: For a domain account enter the domain, for example OFFICE. For an account of a NAS or of another computer you may leave it empty; if access fails, enter the name of that NAS or computer, for example NAS01.

data.name: AccountPasswordNote
data.value: The service keeps the password encrypted (Windows DPAPI) and never shows it again.

data.name: AccountKeepPasswordNote
data.value: Leave the password empty to keep the stored one.

data.name: DefaultLogLevelHelp
data.value: «Totals and errors»: what each run did, and every problem. «Every file»: also the list of copied files; handy to find out what went into a backup, but the logs grow large. A task can choose its own detail.

data.name: CopyPriorityHelp
data.value: Low: copying gives way to the user and to other programs, so the computer does not slow down; while the disk and the processor are free, they are used fully. Normal: faster on a busy computer, but more noticeable.

data.name: ServiceLanguageHelp
data.value: The language of the run logs and of the messages of the service. «Automatic» follows the language of Windows. The window itself follows the language of the user.

data.name: SettingsAccountsNote
data.value: The service keeps the passwords encrypted (Windows DPAPI) and never shows them. An account used by a task cannot be removed.

data.name: SettingsReadOnly
data.value: Only administrators can change the settings.

data.name: ImportNote
data.value: Cobian Backup 11 keeps its tasks in MainList.lst, usually in C:\Program Files (x86)\Cobian Backup 11\DB. The tasks are added switched off: check each one in the editor and switch it on.

data.name: ImportNoRemarks
data.value: Nothing to check: the task was carried over as it is.

data.name: ImportAccounts
data.value: Accounts for network folders («Run as» in Cobian). Enter the password of each one once:

data.name: ImportPasswordRequired
data.value: Enter the password of {0}, or untick the tasks that use it.

data.name: ImportDone
data.value: Tasks imported: {0}. They are switched off: check each one in the editor and switch it on.

data.name: WarnScheduleUnknown
data.value: Unknown schedule type «{0}»: the task is set to run by hand. Set its schedule.

data.name: WarnScheduleNotSupported
data.value: «Once» and «yearly» schedules do not exist in CUSTOS: the task is set to run by hand.

data.name: WarnScheduleAssumed
data.value: The schedule (Cobian code {0}) was read by its most likely meaning: check it on the «Schedule» page.

data.name: WarnTimeUnreadable
data.value: The time of the run could not be read, 00:00 is set: check it.

data.name: WarnWeekdaysAssumed
data.value: Days of the week {0} were read counting Monday as 1: check them on the «Schedule» page.

data.name: WarnBackupTypeAssumed
data.value: The backup type was read as differential: check it.

data.name: WarnBackupTypeNotSupported
data.value: Cobian backup type {0} (for example «dummy») does not exist in CUSTOS: the task is set to full. Check it.

data.name: WarnCompressionAssumed
data.value: The compression type was read as ZIP: check it.

data.name: WarnEncryptionPassword
data.value: The archive is encrypted in Cobian. Its password is not carried over: set it on the «Compression and checks» page, otherwise the task does not run.

data.name: WarnSplitIgnored
data.value: Splitting the archive into volumes was not carried over: set the volume size on the «Compression and checks» page if you need it.

data.name: WarnEventsInComment
data.value: The events before and after were written into the comment: set them again on the «Events» page. {0}

data.name: WarnSourceUnknown
data.value: The entry «{0}» was skipped: its type is unknown or it is not a full path.

data.name: WarnFtpNotSupported
data.value: The FTP entry «{0}» was skipped: CUSTOS does not read from FTP, and writing to FTP arrives in a later version.

data.name: WarnNoSources
data.value: The task has no sources: add them before switching it on.

data.name: WarnNoDestinations
data.value: The task has no destinations: add them before switching it on.

data.name: WarnFixedDayAssumed
data.value: The fixed day of the full backup (Cobian value {0}) was read as a day of the week, counting Monday as 1: check it on the «Basic» page.

data.name: WarnFiltersImported
data.value: Filters were carried over, check them on the «Sources» page: {0}

data.name: WarnRunAsAccount
data.value: In Cobian the task ran as {0}. In CUSTOS this account is used only for the network folders of the task: enter its password below.

data.name: WarnRunAsLocalOnly
data.value: In Cobian the task ran as {0}, but it has no network folders: CUSTOS reads local files as the service, so the account is not needed.

data.name: RestorePasswordNote
data.value: Only for encrypted archives without their task on this computer, or with an older password. Otherwise leave it empty.

data.name: RestoreFound
data.value: Backups found: {0}. Choose the date to restore.

data.name: RestoreToOriginal
data.value: The original places (where the files were copied from)

data.name: RestoreExisting
data.value: If a file is already there:

data.name: RestoreExistingOlder
data.value: Replace it only if it is older

data.name: RestoreChooseTarget
data.value: Choose the folder to restore into.

data.name: RestoreConfirmOriginal
data.value: Restore «{0}» to the original places? Files that are already there stay as they are.

data.name: RestoreConfirmOriginalOverwrite
data.value: Restore «{0}» to the original places? Files that are already there will be replaced.

data.name: RestoreGoesOn
data.value: The restore goes on in the service. Open this window again to see how it ends.

data.name: ArchiveMirrorNote
data.value: A mirror keeps plain files: compression and encryption do not apply to it. Verification does.

data.name: ArchiveZipHelp
data.value: A ZIP archive opens in Windows and in any archiver. Written as a stream, so it suits every kind of destination.

data.name: ArchiveSevenZipHelp
data.value: 7z compresses better and can encrypt the file names. Needs a destination that lets the writer go back in the file: a folder, a network folder or a USB disk.

data.name: ArchiveOpenAnywhere
data.value: Archives stay ordinary 7z and ZIP files: 7-Zip opens them without CUSTOS.

data.name: ArchiveLevelHelp
data.value: Higher levels make smaller archives but take longer. Level 5 is the usual balance.

data.name: ArchiveSplitHelp
data.value: 7z only. The volumes are name.7z.001, .002 …; 7-Zip opens them from the first one.

data.name: ArchiveEncryptNames
data.value: Encrypt the file names too (7z only)

data.name: ArchiveEncryptNamesHelp
data.value: Without the password nobody even sees which files the archive holds.

data.name: ArchivePasswordWarning
data.value: Write the password down and keep it apart from the backups: without it the archives cannot be opened by anyone, CUSTOS included.

data.name: ArchivePasswordChangeNote
data.value: Archives made before keep the old password: keep it too, you will need it to restore them.

data.name: ArchivePasswordRequired
data.value: Encryption is on: set the password (button «Password…»).

data.name: ArchiveSevenZipNeedsSeek
data.value: 7z cannot be written to {0}: choose ZIP or no compression for this task.

data.name: VerifyEveryRuns
data.value: Verify the new backup every N-th run:

data.name: VerifyEveryRunsHelp
data.value: 0 = never, 1 = every run. Archives are unpacked into nowhere with their checksums checked; plain copies are read back and compared. Nothing is written to disk.

data.name: VerifyStoredDays
data.value: Verify all stored backups every N days:

data.name: VerifyStoredDaysHelp
data.value: 0 = off. Done after a successful run when the time has come. A damaged backup makes the run an error.

data.name: Settings7ZipNote
data.value: The button looks at the official 7-Zip releases on GitHub only when pressed, and updates only after you agree. By hand: stop the CUSTOS service, replace 7z.dll in the CUSTOS program folder with the one from the 64-bit 7-Zip, start the service.

data.name: PowerCountdownText
data.value: The task «{0}» has finished. In {2} s: {1}.

data.name: PowerCancelFailed
data.value: The service did not cancel it.

data.name: PathVariablesNote
data.value: The path may hold variables: %USERPROFILE%, %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, %OneDrive% (of whoever saved the task first), other Windows variables like %SystemDrive%, and {computer}, {task}, {yyyy}, {MM}, {dd}.

data.name: PreserveAcl
data.value: Keep NTFS permissions of files and folders

data.name: PreserveAclHelp
data.value: For copies without compression: files and folders in the copy get the permissions and the owner of the originals. If a destination does not take them (some network folders), the files are still copied and the run gets a warning. FAT and exFAT disks keep no permissions.

data.name: SevenZipNothingNew
data.value: You have 7-Zip {0}; the newest is {1}. There is nothing to update.

data.name: SevenZipAskUpdate
data.value:
You have 7-Zip {0}; the newest is {1}.
Update now? The service downloads the 64-bit installer from the official 7-Zip page on GitHub, checks its SHA-256, takes 7z.dll from it, tests it and only then replaces the old file (kept as 7z.dll.old). Tasks wait meanwhile; it takes about a minute.

data.name: DatabasesNote
data.value: Databases of MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL on this computer (for example of OSPanel) are dumped whole in every run, by the server's own programs, into the folder «db» of each copy. The data folder of a server need not be copied as files. For MS SQL or 1C, add a program to «Events» that makes the dump into a source folder.

data.name: DbBinDirHelp
data.value: The bin folder of the server, with mysqldump and mysql (MariaDB: mariadb-dump and mariadb; PostgreSQL: pg_dump, pg_dumpall and psql). For OSPanel 6 it is like C:\OSPanel\modules\MySQL-8.0\bin. «Find» looks for running servers and the usual folders.

data.name: DbHostHelp
data.value: Where the server listens. OSPanel 6 gives each module an address of its own, like 127.127.126.26; «Find» takes it from the running server.

data.name: DbAccountNote
data.value: An account that may read every database: root for MySQL and MariaDB, postgres for PostgreSQL. The password is kept by the service, encrypted.

data.name: DbKeepPasswordNote
data.value: Leave the password empty to keep the stored one.

data.name: DbListNote
data.value: The list fills in on «Test connection». A ticked database goes into the copy: with «All databases» untick one to leave it out, new databases are added by themselves. System databases are never dumped as databases; users and rights go to _users.sql.

data.name: ErrorDbBinDirRequired
data.value: Choose the folder of the server's programs.

data.name: ErrorDbHostRequired
data.value: Enter the address of the server.

data.name: ErrorDbNothingChosen
data.value: Tick at least one database, or choose «All databases».

data.name: DbFindNothing
data.value: No MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL was found. Choose the folder of the programs yourself.

data.name: DbFindNote
data.value: Running servers come first, with the address they listen on. Pick one and press OK.

data.name: RestoreDumpsNote
data.value: The set has database dumps. They are restored as .sql files into the folder «db» with README.txt on how to load them; CUSTOS does not load them into a server. Without a folder they are not restored.
